_law: BRIGHT LINES are GLOBAL and non-negotiable (they live in cast.json shared_rules - safety never varies by format). Everything else - room laws, tone, segment architecture, transitions - belongs to the SHOW TYPE. Producer and cast are INDEPENDENT of type: the same cast can run any type; the type is the FORMAT the room runs tonight. Robert 2026-08-31: think Maddow vs hot-take vs panel - different rooms, different laws.

types.name: THE PANEL
types.inspiration: Multi-host clash - the room argues it out (our proven floor engine)
laws: Disagreement is engineered by the beat sheet; agreement is earned, never automatic
Turn lengths UNEVEN - jabs beat paragraphs; the allocator decides who talks
Interruptions land mid-clause; losing a floor bid = backchannel
Withheld receipts detonate ON the floor; reveals are live
Somebody lands a verdict; the exit is a tease, never a fade

segments.name: COLD OPEN
segments.role: hottest take commits in two sentences; show ID in one breath
segments.transition: hard cut - one stinger hit into the floor

segments.name: THE FLOOR
segments.role: the lead topic argued; stances locked, receipts flowing

segments.name: THE RECEIPT
segments.role: withheld evidence lands; genuine live reaction
segments.transition: beat of silence, then the elder clears his throat

types.name: THE DESK
types.inspiration: Maddow-style: one anchor builds the case piece by piece, segmented
laws: Measured, never shouty - authority comes from the BUILD, not volume
Every block opens with context that seems unrelated, then the turn connects it
Receipts are read ON AIR ('here is what the post actually says')
Rhetorical questions the anchor answers; direct address to camera
Each block ends one step short of the conclusion - the audience closes the loop

segments.name: A-BLOCK
segments.role: the day's lead as a built case: context -> receipts -> the turn
segments.transition: three receipt beats, then 'and that brings us to tonight'

segments.name: B-BLOCK
segments.role: second story or the lead's consequence thread

segments.name: C-BLOCK
segments.role: lighter: the culture item, the birthday, the follow-up watch
segments.transition: tone lift - one honest laugh allowed

segments.name: THE LAST WORD
segments.role: anchor's verdict + what to watch tomorrow

types.name: THE TAKE
types.inspiration: One loud opinion-driver defends a single thesis (the hot-take single)
laws: ONE thesis, stated in the first ten seconds, defended to the death
Direct address; dares the audience to disagree
Concessions exist only to set up counterpunches
Numbers and receipts delivered like punchlines
Ends by planting the flag harder than it started

segments.name: THE THESIS
segments.transition: repeat the thesis word once, quieter

segments.name: THE RUN
segments.role: receipts machine-gunned in service of the thesis
segments.transition: 'but let me guess what you're typing right now'

segments.name: THE COUNTERPUNCH
segments.role: steelman the objection, then break it

segments.name: THE FLAG
segments.role: restate the thesis harder + the dare

types.name: THE HOT WIRE
types.inspiration: Fast roundup + caller drop-ins (the phone-EQ voice is a FEATURE here)
types.cast_shape: 1-2 hosts + designed 'caller' voices (acoustic_attributes: phone quality on purpose)
laws: Speed - no item over 60 seconds
Jokes land or the item dies; one-liners over analysis
Callers sound like CALLERS (phone-bandwidth designed voices, interrupted freely)
The wire never apologizes for moving on
Solo items (birthdays, tags, announcements) LIVE here

segments.name: THE OPEN
segments.role: what the wire is carrying today, rapid-fire list

segments.name: THE CALLER
segments.role: a designed phone-voice character with one unhinged take

segments.name: THE CLOSE
segments.role: the one thing to watch + out
